togetherJourney.title: Take an idea further, together.
togetherJourney.intro: Choose a topic in Explore, try a small challenge with someone, and see how a learning companion could reflect your progress. This is a sample journey.

nature.title: Notice a tiny change outside
nature.body: Take the nature activity into your neighbourhood. You and a friend can notice different things, then compare them.
nature.try: Look closely at one plant or outdoor spot.
nature.compare: Ask a friend what they noticed that you missed.
nature.explain: Tell each other one question you want to explore next.

stories.title: Tell the same story two ways
stories.body: Start with a story idea and discover how another person's point of view changes it.
stories.try: Choose a character and imagine their first line.
stories.compare: Ask a friend to tell the moment from another character's view.

science.title: Build, test, improve
science.body: Try a simple paper structure together and compare which shapes help it stand.
science.compare: Compare it with a friend's different design.
science.explain: Explain one change you would test next.

nature.title: How does a seed grow?
nature.body: Notice the small changes in the plants around you.
nature.materials: Paper and pencil. Ask a volunteer to join you outdoors or look at a potted plant.
steps: Look closely at one plant without picking it.
Draw one leaf and note its shape or colour.
Compare your drawing with what you can see.
nature.reflection: What detail did you notice first? Next, browse a nature book or tell a volunteer what you observed. Do not taste plants or touch unknown plants.

stories.title: Every place has a story.
stories.body: Imagine a new adventure in a familiar place.
stories.materials: No special materials. You can tell the story aloud or use paper and pencil.
steps: Choose an imaginary character and a familiar place.
Imagine one person they meet and one kind thing they do.
Tell or sketch what happens next.
stories.reflection: Which part would you like to change or continue? Next, browse a story book or share your idea with a volunteer.

science.title: What makes a bridge strong?
science.body: Explore shapes using a little paper and curiosity.
science.materials: One sheet of paper, two books, and a few small paper pieces. Ask a volunteer to help set up.
steps: Place a flat sheet across two books set close together.
Add one small paper piece at a time and notice what happens.
Fold a fresh sheet into a simple fan shape and compare using the same light paper pieces.
science.reflection: Which shape held more paper, and what might explain that? Next, browse a science book or tell a volunteer what changed. Keep the books on a table and use only light paper.
